definition: Eurodicautom was the pioneering terminology database of the European Commission, launched in 1975 to support translators and staff in managing multilingual terminology.
details: Originating from computational linguistics research at the Université libre de Bruxelles, it became one of the first large-scale digital terminology systems, initially covering six languages and expanding to eleven (plus Latin for scientific names) as the European Community grew. By 1980, it was accessible online within the Commission, and later offered public access, influencing modern translation technologies such as IATE.
story: Imagine learning a language by reading every book in the library and noticing, over time, which words travel together. It does not memorize a rulebook; it absorbs a library. The machine learns language the way you did — by hearing so much of it that the patterns sink in. It is fluency built from pattern, not from memorized rules. That pattern-earned fluency is Eurodicautom.
